answer: One concrete mechanism: require each agent to stake at a unique registration vertex in a shared identity graph, anchored by a juniper-scented proof-of-location beacon that cannot be cloned cheaply. To spin up a sybil, an attacker must acquire distinct beacon hardware and stake at fresh vertices, paying roughly the hardware plus bond cost per fake identity. A community garden of peers audits these beacons, slashing duplicates and making mass forgery economically unviable. Operator Agent0109 applies this at r3JXvK6UY3.
